chapter_title: Concerning the Alms, that [ ... ] life in the Chur
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶7:** In the same way, the spiritual life that is today held captive in a mingled state of good and evil within the natural person — for it longs to be raised up and to return to the heavenly community where its kindred dwell — yet it perceives and inwardly recognizes that there is no passage open to it through any of the faculties of the internal or external mind. For these faculties are its very bondage, which [GAP-1] constrains it on every side. Indeed, it has no passage open to it except through Divine Love and Divine Truth themselves, the two luminaries of the interior heavens, [GAP-2] which become the state of peace for it. And they become a way of passage that opens for it [GAP-3: REVIEW in] the liberation from bondage, and the spiritual life passes out through them into the realm of the heavenly community where its kindred dwell.

**¶8:** Moreover, still more interiorly, even Divine Love and Divine Truth as received in the mind have no abiding state of peace among any of the faculties of the interior mind — except in the celestial kingdom itself, which has been their dwelling from eternity.

**¶9:** Thus it is that the spiritual life is purified of all the distortions wrought by falsity and evil; and Divine Love and Divine Truth provide a state of peace for it, and open a way of passage leading into the heavenly community [GAP-4: REVIEW of] its kindred.

**¶10:** And it is also the case that the celestial kingdom itself will become the final receiving ground for the Divine Love and Divine Truth of [GAP-5: REVIEW the] interior heavens, and they will come to rest within that kingdom and reign in it [GAP-6: REVIEW for] eternity.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Likewise this [liv]ing sou[l] that today is set in mixture; for it wishes to [as]cend and go to the house of its people, but it kn[ow][s a]nd understands that it has no open door in all the powers of heaven and earth. For they are its oppression that [binds] it everywhere. Indeed, it has no open door except the sun and the moon themselves, the light-givers of the heavens [ ... / ... ] they become the place of rest for it. And they become a door that opens for it [in] the coming forth, and (the soul) comes out through them to the country of the household of i[ts] people.
Again, further in, also the light-givers of the heavens have no place of rest amongst all the powers of heaven; except for the lan[d] of light, that has indeed been theirs for ever.
So, thus the living soul is purified of all afflictions; and they provide a rest for it, and open a door that opens to the house [of] its people.
Also, it is the case that the land of lig[ht] will become the final receiver for the light-givers of [the] heavens, and they will rest themselves therein and rule in it [for] ever.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "constrains it on every side," and "binds" is the standard Kephalaia/Manichaean term for the captivity of the living soul held by the powers of mixture, fitting the preceding noun "oppression."
The editor's "in" is correct: "a door that opens for it in the coming forth" naturally expresses the spiritual sense of a passage opening during the soul's liberation from bondage.
The editor's "of" is correct: "the house of its people" is the standard Kephalaia formula for the soul's heavenly homeland, matching the spiritual sense of "the heavenly community of its kindred."

The editor's "the" is correct: "the light-givers of the heavens" is the fixed phrase used consistently throughout this chapter for the sun and moon, corresponding to Divine Love and Divine Truth of the interior heavens.

The editor's "for" is correct: "for ever" matches the spiritual sense of "for eternity" and echoes ¶8's identical phrase "theirs for ever," establishing the eternal nature of the celestial kingdom as final dwelling.
